name: The Client Gauntlet
purpose: Build confidence and judgement in difficult client conversations.
methods: AI role-play; live actor; triad practice; video review
mechanics: Observation; deliberate practice; feedback; variability; transfer-appropriate practice
setup: Three practice rooms or stations; private replay spaces
needs: 1 lead facilitator; 1 coach per 6–8 learners; governed AI scenarios; consent for recording
outputs: Before/after performance evidence; personal practice plan; reusable scenario bank
bestUse: Sales, consulting, discovery, executive influence
cautions: Do not use generic personas; calibrate AI feedback against expert standards; protect psychological safety.

name: The Live Challenge
purpose: Apply learning to a real unresolved business need.
methods: Live case; field study; design sprint; studio critique
mechanics: Authenticity; generation; social learning; feedback; transfer
setup: Team studios; sponsor touchpoints; prototype materials
needs: Named sponsor; access to real evidence/users; design facilitators; implementation owner
outputs: Tested concept; decision memo; 30-day implementation experiment
bestUse: Innovation, transformation and capability academies
cautions: Sponsor must genuinely need the work; clarify confidentiality, decision rights and what happens after the retreat.

name: The Learning Residency
purpose: Develop deep craft, professional identity and a strong cohort.
methods: Residency; studio; masterclass; critique; reflection
mechanics: Cognitive apprenticeship; feedback; identity; consolidation; social accountability
setup: Dedicated studio left intact overnight; exhibition wall
needs: Expert practitioners who can model and critique; generous making time; optional evening programme
outputs: Portfolio artefacts; revised work; community rituals; long-term craft goal
bestUse: Design, strategy, storytelling and leadership craft
cautions: Do not over-program. The value comes from protected practice, expert access and revision.

name: The Failure Lab
purpose: Use bounded failure to expose misconceptions and improve strategy.
methods: Productive failure; error analysis; contrast cases; retry
mechanics: Generation; productive failure; feedback; metacognition; contrast
setup: Team tables; visible work wall; private data capture
needs: Facilitator skilled in non-blaming debrief; carefully engineered task; clear expert model
outputs: Failure patterns; revised strategy; before/after work sample
bestUse: Problem framing, innovation, systems and decision quality
cautions: Failure must be informative, safe and followed by explicit instruction. Never manufacture humiliation.

name: The Future Simulation
purpose: Rehearse strategic decisions across plausible futures.
methods: Scenario planning; business simulation; role-play; red teaming
mechanics: Narrative; variability; emotion regulation; reflection; transfer
setup: Separate scenario rooms or zones; central mission control
needs: Scenario writers; control team issuing injects; consequence model; expert debrief
outputs: No-regret moves; signposts; decision principles; risk log
bestUse: Strategy, AI disruption, resilience and operating-model change
cautions: Scenarios are not forecasts. Avoid theatrical detail that hides assumptions or overwhelms decisions.

name: The Skill Arcade
purpose: Build several related micro-skills through high-variety stations.
methods: Learning stations; drills; clinics; mastery checks
mechanics: Deliberate practice; interleaving; feedback; autonomy; mastery
setup: 5–10 clearly branded stations; central orientation and recovery area
needs: Station facilitator per 6–10; common rubrics; timing and movement support
outputs: Individual skill profile; completed challenge cards; follow-up drill prescription
bestUse: Large cohorts needing active practice without plenary monotony
cautions: Transitions consume time. Standardise criteria while allowing different practice routes.

name: The Field Expedition
purpose: Ground learning in real environments and evidence.
methods: Field study; learning walk; ethnographic observation; studio synthesis
mechanics: Situated learning; attention; curiosity; reflection; transfer
setup: Real site plus a nearby synthesis space
needs: Permissions, ethics and accessibility plan; observation guides; transport; local hosts
outputs: Evidence wall; insights; opportunity backlog; questions for experimentation
bestUse: Customer experience, systems, service and operational learning
cautions: Do not treat people as exhibits. Manage consent, confidentiality, safety and observer bias.

name: The Capability Launch
purpose: Launch a sustained capability pathway rather than a one-off event.
methods: Cohort; simulation; project; coaching; spacing; portfolio
mechanics: Spacing; social accountability; mastery; implementation intentions; transfer
setup: Retreat venue plus digital cohort hub and scheduled follow-ups
needs: Programme owner; managers; coaches; assessment rubrics; community lead
outputs: Verified workplace outcomes; portfolio; capability data; continuing community
bestUse: AI, leadership, sales or role academies
cautions: Secure managers and project opportunities before launch. Do not measure only attendance and satisfaction.

name: The Executive Decision Room
purpose: Improve evidence use, challenge and decision quality.
methods: Decision-forcing case; fishbowl; red team; premortem
mechanics: Generation; calibration; social learning; cognitive conflict; feedforward
setup: Boardroom layout with visible evidence and decision log
needs: Credible case; neutral facilitator; explicit challenge protocol; senior sponsor
outputs: Decision rationale; assumptions; risk mitigations; challenge norms
bestUse: Strategy, investments, governance and transformation decisions
cautions: Status can silence dissent. Require individual commitment before group discussion and protect minority views.

name: The Unconference Studio
purpose: Use participant expertise while still producing coherent outputs.
methods: Open Space; peer teaching; studio work; gallery critique
mechanics: Autonomy; social learning; generation; identity; accountability
setup: Large marketplace plus multiple breakout studios and exhibition space
needs: Strong convening question; session templates; documentation stewards; synthesis facilitators
outputs: Community-owned playbook; prototypes; named practice groups
bestUse: Communities of practice and capability festivals
cautions: Run after shared foundations. Without synthesis and ownership it becomes a collection of interesting conversations.

name: The Simulation Ladder
purpose: Progress from safe rehearsal to realistic integrated performance.
methods: Worked example; low/high-fidelity simulation; role-play; coaching
mechanics: Scaffolding; fading; deliberate practice; variability; delayed feedback
setup: Practice rooms of increasing realism; observation area
needs: Scenario control; trained actors or facilitators; common performance criteria
outputs: Competency profile; recorded capstone; targeted follow-up plan
bestUse: Interpersonal, operational and safety-critical capability
cautions: Higher fidelity is not automatically better. Increase realism only when it adds relevant cues or consequences.

name: The Mastery Circuit
purpose: Ensure every learner reaches a minimum practical standard.
methods: Diagnostic; mastery learning; clinics; stations; reassessment
mechanics: Mastery; feedback; retrieval; autonomy; scaffolding
setup: Multiple routes with clear signage; assessment and remediation zones
needs: Validated criteria; assessors calibrated; enough coaches and time for retries
outputs: Verified mastery record; individual gap report; extension challenge
bestUse: Technical, regulatory and prerequisite skills
cautions: A mastery programme needs genuine reassessment capacity. Avoid arbitrary pass marks and quiz-only evidence.

name: The Challenge Tournament
purpose: Generate many possibilities, then improve selection quality.
methods: Innovation tournament; pitch; peer marketplace; prototype
mechanics: Generation; contrast; social learning; feedback; reinforcement
setup: Large plenary, team bays, visible tournament board
needs: Transparent criteria; diverse judges; small experiment budget; anti-bias process
outputs: Prioritised portfolio; experiment charters; evidence gaps
bestUse: Innovation portfolios, sustainability and process improvement
cautions: Competition can reward charisma and familiarity. Separate idea quality from presentation polish and fund tests, not winners.

name: The Story Lab
purpose: Develop persuasive, evidence-grounded stories through repeated crafting and performance.
methods: Storytelling; studio; video review; peer critique
mechanics: Narrative; retrieval; feedback; deliberate practice; identity
setup: Quiet writing space, small story circles and recording booths
needs: Story coach; evidence and ethics guidance; recording consent; editing support
outputs: Three-minute story; longer written version; personal story bank
bestUse: Client storytelling, leadership and change communication
cautions: Do not force disclosure or substitute emotion for evidence. Avoid making every story follow one formula.

name: The Facilitation Flight School
purpose: Build facilitation skill through increasingly difficult live situations.
methods: Behavioural modelling; deliberate practice; live simulation; video review
mechanics: Observation; practice; immediate feedback; variability; reflection
setup: Flexible workshop room; breakout rooms; cameras optional
needs: Expert facilitators; trained role players; shared rubric; high psychological safety
outputs: Facilitation reel; practice plan; response library for difficult moments
bestUse: Workshop, design and leadership facilitation
cautions: Review behaviour, not personality. Recording must be optional or tightly governed.

name: The AI Practice Studio
purpose: Use AI for high-volume personalised rehearsal with human quality control.
methods: AI tutor; AI role-play; personalised scenario generation; expert coaching
mechanics: Deliberate practice; variability; feedback; metacognition; transfer
setup: Headsets and private spaces; approved AI environment; expert clinic area
needs: Governed prompts and data; human rubric; technical support; bias and privacy guidance
outputs: Practice transcripts; calibrated feedback; personal prompt/scenario kit
bestUse: Sales, leadership, language and communication practice
cautions: Treat model feedback as a hypothesis, not truth. Never expose confidential client or employee data.

name: The Systems War Room
purpose: Understand a complex system and rehearse interventions.
methods: Systems mapping; simulation; red teaming; live case
mechanics: Elaboration; embodied cognition; cognitive conflict; transfer
setup: Large wall or floor map; movable tokens; control desk
needs: Systems facilitator; reliable data; representatives from affected functions
outputs: Shared system model; leverage points; experiment portfolio; assumptions log
bestUse: Operating models, service systems and transformation
cautions: A map is a model, not reality. Keep uncertainty visible and include voices affected by decisions.

name: The Crisis Command Exercise
purpose: Rehearse coordinated response under time pressure.
methods: Tabletop; live simulation; role-play; AAR
mechanics: Transfer-appropriate practice; emotion regulation; team cognition; reflection
setup: Mission-control room, role tables, live incident log
needs: Control team; observers; tested injects; clear stop rules; wellbeing and accessibility options
outputs: Response log; role gaps; revised protocol; follow-up practice plan
bestUse: Cyber, business continuity, reputational and client crises
cautions: Do not confuse stress with fidelity. Protect wellbeing and separate developmental learning from blame.

name: The Leadership Mirror
purpose: Make leadership behaviour visible through multiple perspectives.
methods: Assessment centre; role-play; coaching; peer feedback
mechanics: Calibration; feedback; observation; self-explanation; feedforward
setup: One task room, observation space and private coaching rooms
needs: Qualified coaches; behavioural rubric; consent and confidentiality protocol
outputs: Behavioural strengths and risks; one tested change; coach follow-up plan
bestUse: Leadership transitions and developmental programmes
cautions: This is developmental, not covert performance assessment. Avoid personality judgements and protect confidentiality.

name: The Learning Festival
purpose: Create breadth, energy and self-directed exploration across a community.
methods: Festival; marketplace; Open Space; skill arcade; showcases
mechanics: Autonomy; curiosity; social learning; identity; relevance
setup: Zoned venue with quiet, active, demo and reflection spaces
needs: Programme curation; production team; session hosts; accessible navigation; digital schedule
outputs: Connections; sampled skills; community content; pathway enrolments
bestUse: Capability awareness, community building and cross-pollination
cautions: A festival creates energy but not mastery. Always connect it to deeper pathways and make quiet, accessible alternatives available.

name: The Reverse Classroom Retreat
purpose: Maximise precious co-located time for practice rather than presentation.
methods: Flipped learning; retrieval; clinics; simulation; spacing
mechanics: Retrieval; cognitive load; feedback; mastery; transfer
setup: Minimal plenary seating; many practice and clinic spaces
needs: High-quality concise pre-work; completion support; diagnostics; coaches
outputs: Corrected misconceptions; applied work; individual follow-up path
bestUse: Programmes where foundational knowledge can be learned before travel
cautions: Do not push hours of content into pre-work. Design an equitable route for those who could not complete it.

name: The Expert Fishbowl
purpose: Expose expert judgement and invite disciplined challenge.
methods: Fishbowl; think-aloud; case method; peer instruction
mechanics: Observation; self-explanation; contrast; retrieval; feedback
setup: Central circle with observer worksheets and group tables
needs: Experts capable of verbalising uncertainty; skilled moderator; strong case
outputs: Visible decision heuristics; participant solution; questions for practice
bestUse: Tacit professional judgement and complex case work
cautions: Avoid guru theatre. Use multiple experts and make disagreement, uncertainty and limits visible.

name: The Evidence Courtroom
purpose: Strengthen evidence assessment and argument quality.
methods: Debate; role-play; case method; comparative judgement
mechanics: Elaboration; cognitive conflict; social learning; metacognition
setup: Courtroom-style room; evidence tables; jury area
needs: Balanced evidence packs; moderator; argument and evidence rubric
outputs: Claim map; evidence quality assessment; revised recommendation
bestUse: Critical thinking, research literacy and decision-making
cautions: Do not reward rhetoric over evidence. Build in role rotation and individual reflection after the performance.

name: The Museum of Mistakes
purpose: Learn from errors without exposing individuals to blame.
methods: Curated exhibition; critical incident; gallery walk; clinic
mechanics: Contrast; error management; reflection; social learning
setup: Exhibition space with anonymised artefacts and redesign tables
needs: Ethical curation; anonymisation; facilitators trained in just culture
outputs: Failure-pattern taxonomy; prevention and recovery practices; updated job aids
bestUse: Operational learning, quality and project delivery
cautions: Anonymisation must be credible. Include successful recoveries as well as failures and avoid hindsight bias.

name: The Customer Reality Lab
purpose: Build empathy and better decisions from customer evidence, not assumption.
methods: Customer immersion; service safari; role-play; prototype testing
mechanics: Situated learning; attention; generation; feedback; relevance
setup: Evidence gallery, interview rooms and prototype studio
needs: Ethics and consent; customer evidence; research facilitator; testing access
outputs: Revised journey; assumption log; tested service improvement
bestUse: Customer experience and service transformation
cautions: Do not use one customer as a universal persona. Distinguish evidence, interpretation and assumption.

name: The Negotiation Dojo
purpose: Develop negotiation moves through short repeated bouts and review.
methods: Role-play; deliberate practice; simulation; coaching
mechanics: Practice; variability; feedback; emotional regulation; calibration
setup: Multiple small rooms; timers; private preparation space
needs: Negotiation coach; balanced briefs; observers; common criteria
outputs: Negotiation strategy; personal tendencies; tested alternative moves
bestUse: Commercial, stakeholder and internal negotiation
cautions: Do not equate aggression with skill. Brief power differences and ethical boundaries explicitly.

name: The Prototype Marketplace
purpose: Learn by making multiple solutions visible and testable.
methods: Prototyping; gallery walk; peer marketplace; critique
mechanics: Generation; feedback; contrast; embodied cognition; social learning
setup: Large room with team stalls, prototype materials and feedback tokens
needs: Clear test questions; diverse testers; rapid-making materials; timekeeper
outputs: Multiple prototypes; test evidence; revised concept; reusable patterns
bestUse: Service, product, process and learning design
cautions: Market popularity is not evidence of impact. Define what each prototype is testing.

name: The Manager Transfer Lab
purpose: Equip managers to make learning stick after the retreat.
methods: Transfer planning; coaching; implementation intentions; social accountability
mechanics: Implementation intentions; relevance; feedforward; habit and cue design
setup: Paired seating with private planning space
needs: Manager briefing; transfer templates; escalation route; scheduled follow-up
outputs: Manager–learner contract; protected practice time; review date; barrier plan
bestUse: Any programme where workplace conditions determine application
cautions: Managers must not turn development evidence into punitive evaluation. Resolve system barriers, not just learner motivation.

name: The Reflection Observatory
purpose: Develop metacognition and integrate intensive experiences.
methods: Silent reflection; journalling; peer reflection; concept mapping
mechanics: Reflection; consolidation; calibration; implementation intentions; identity
setup: Quiet individual zones plus optional walking route and paired spaces
needs: Carefully designed prompts; accessible alternatives; no forced disclosure
outputs: Revised mental model; decision journal; commitments; personal narrative
bestUse: Multi-day retreats and emotionally or cognitively intense programmes
cautions: Reflection should use evidence and lead to changed action. Do not force intimacy or public disclosure.

name: The Knowledge Expedition
purpose: Turn research into collective understanding and usable practice.
methods: Research sprint; reciprocal teaching; concept mapping; teach-back
mechanics: Retrieval; elaboration; social learning; metacognition; dual coding
setup: Source library, research stations, large evidence map
needs: Curated credible sources; research librarian or expert; synthesis templates
outputs: Evidence map; field guide; unanswered questions; source index
bestUse: AI, regulation, emerging technology and new market understanding
cautions: Control source quality and separate consensus from evidence. Avoid dividing research so narrowly nobody sees the whole.

name: The Peer Consultancy
purpose: Use the cohort to solve one another’s real challenges with disciplined inquiry.
methods: Action learning; peer coaching; case clinic
mechanics: Social learning; self-explanation; feedforward; accountability; transfer
setup: Small circles; visible question protocol; no-slide rule
needs: Strong contracting; trained set facilitator; follow-up schedule
outputs: Experiment plan for each owner; peer support network; evidence review
bestUse: Leadership, project and client-delivery challenges
cautions: Peers must ask before advising. Manage confidentiality and avoid turning the session into ungrounded consultancy.

name: The Observatory and Control Room
purpose: Teach system monitoring and intervention through live data.
methods: Digital twin; simulation; team cognition; AAR
mechanics: Attention; transfer-appropriate practice; feedback; contextual interference
setup: Control-room layout with shared dashboards and role stations
needs: Realistic data model; scenario controller; observer rubric; technical support
outputs: Signal library; intervention protocol; handover checklist; team gaps
bestUse: Operations, cyber, product reliability and service management
cautions: Do not overload with decorative dashboards. Metrics and consequences must reflect the real system.

name: The Ethical Dilemma Forum
purpose: Develop principled judgement where rules do not provide an easy answer.
methods: Dilemma case; role-play; fishbowl; structured dialogue
mechanics: Generation; cognitive conflict; perspective-taking; reflection; identity
setup: Circle seating plus stakeholder breakout areas
needs: Ethics facilitator; nuanced cases; ground rules; escalation and support routes
outputs: Decision principles; unresolved tensions; policy questions; individual rationale
bestUse: AI ethics, professional standards, inclusion and governance
cautions: Avoid false binaries and moral theatre. Protect minority perspectives and separate legal requirements from ethical judgement.
